input.code: import json import re from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse # ── hard safety caps ───────────────────────────────────────── RAW_INPUT_HARD_CAP = 200_000 # never process more raw chars than this MAX_CANDIDATE_LINKS = 40 # never return more than this many links MAX_LINKS_JSON_CHARS = 8_000 # hard cap on the final event_urls_json string def main(input_data): # ── Parse Input ────────────────────────────────────────────── if isinstance(input_data, str): try: input_data = json.loads(input_data) except: pass # Accept markdown directly OR html as fallback raw_markdown = ( input_data.get('markdown', '') or input_data.get('data', '') or input_data.get('html', '') if isinstance(input_data, dict) else str(input_data) ) # ── NEW: normalize to str — fixes # "TypeError: cannot use a string pattern on a bytes-like object" # Some upstream responses (e.g. raw/compressed HTTP bodies) can # come through as bytes instead of str. re.sub() with a str # pattern crashes on bytes input, so decode defensively here, # before any length checks or regex processing happens. if isinstance(raw_markdown, bytes): raw_markdown = raw_markdown.decode('utf-8', errors='replace') elif not isinstance(raw_markdown, str): raw_markdown = str(raw_markdown) source_url = ( input_data.get('source_url', 'http://example.com') if isinstance(input_data, dict) else 'http://example.com' ) try: max_length = int(input_data.get('max_length', 30000)) if isinstance(input_data, dict) else 30000 except (ValueError, TypeError): max_length = 30000 # ── NEW: detect binary/non-text content (PDF, images, archives, etc.) # disguised as a hex-encoded string. This happens when the upstream # scraper fetches a file (not an HTML page) and content_type is null, # so the binary body gets serialized as a hex string like # "0x255044462d312e37..." (which decodes to "%PDF-1.7..."). # Without this check, hundreds of KB of meaningless hex get truncated, # "cleaned", and sent to Claude as if it were real page content — # wasting tokens/cost on every PDF/binary URL that slips through. if _looks_like_binary_hex(raw_markdown): try: _domain = urlparse(source_url).netloc.replace('www.', '') except: _domain = "" return { "success": True, "cleaned_text": "", "source_url": source_url, "source_domain": _domain, "event_urls": [], "event_urls_json": "[]", "urls_with_text": 0, "urls_without_text": 0, "reason": "Source content is binary (PDF/image/archive), not a webpage", "original_length": len(raw_markdown), "cleaned_length": 0, "log": "Skipped - binary/non-text content detected (likely PDF or similar file)" } # ── NEW: hard-cap raw_markdown BEFORE any processing ───────── # This is the actual fix for the 1.4M-token bug: link extraction # used to run on the FULL uncapped raw_markdown, even though # cleaned_text was already capped at max_length. A pathological # page (broken render, sitemap, infinite listing) could produce # megabytes of raw_markdown and thousands of extracted links. raw_input_was_truncated = False if len(raw_markdown) > RAW_INPUT_HARD_CAP: raw_markdown = raw_markdown[:RAW_INPUT_HARD_CAP] raw_input_was_truncated = True # ── Excluded domains ───────────────────────────────────────── excluded_domains = [ # Western social 'facebook.com', 'fb.com', 'fb.watch', 'twitter.com', 'x.com', 'instagram.com', 'whatsapp.com', 'youtube.com', 'youtu.be', 'tiktok.com', 'tinyurl.com', 'linkedin.com', 't.me', 'telegram.org', 'discord.com', 'discord.gg', # Chinese social 'weixin.qq.com', 'mp.weixin.qq.com', 'weibo.com', 'douyin.com', 'bilibili.com', 'zhihu.com', 'xiaohongshu.com', 'tieba.baidu.com', 'kuaishou.com', 'ixigua.com', ] # ── Excluded extensions ────────────────────────────────────── excluded_extensions = [ '.pdf', '.doc', '.docx', '.odt', '.rtf', '.txt', '.pages', '.xls', '.xlsx', '.csv', '.ods', '.ppt', '.pptx', '.odp', '.zip', '.rar', '.7z' ] # ── Excluded navigation/legal text ─────────────────────────── exclude_text_kw = [ # English 'privacy policy', 'terms of use', 'terms of service', 'cookie policy', 'cookie notice', 'log in', 'sign in', 'create account', 'contact us', 'about us', 'report vulnerability', 'feedback', # Chinese '隐私政策', '用户协议', '服务条款', '使用条款', '关于我们', '联系我们', '登录', '注册账号', '意见反馈', '帮助中心', '常见问题', '版权声明', '免责声明', '网站地图', ] exclude_path_kw = [ 'privacy', 'terms', 'login', 'signin', 'signup', 'account', 'contact', 'about', 'cookie', 'legal', 'help', 'faq', 'support', 'sitemap', ] # ── Empty input guard ──────────────────────────────────────── if not raw_markdown: return { "success": False, "cleaned_text": "", "source_url": source_url, "source_domain": "", "event_urls": [], "event_urls_json": "[]", "urls_with_text": 0, "urls_without_text": 0, "reason": "No content provided", "original_length": 0, "cleaned_length": 0, "log": "No content provided" } original_length = len(raw_markdown) # ── Extract source domain ──────────────────────────────────── try: source_domain = urlparse(source_url).netloc.replace('www.', '') except: source_domain = "" # ── Block social media sources ─────────────────────────────── if any(ex in source_domain for ex in excluded_domains): return { "success": True, "cleaned_text": "", "source_url": source_url, "source_domain": source_domain, "event_urls": [], "event_urls_json": "[]", "urls_with_text": 0, "urls_without_text": 0, "reason": "Source URL is social media ({})".format(source_domain), "original_length": original_length, "cleaned_length": 0, "log": "Skipped - social media source: {}".format(source_domain) } # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # STEP 1: Clean the Markdown # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ cleaned = _clean_markdown(raw_markdown, max_length) cleaned_length = len(cleaned) # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # STEP 2: Extract candidate links from Markdown # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ candidate_links, stats = _extract_links_from_markdown( raw_markdown, source_url, source_domain, excluded_domains, excluded_extensions, exclude_text_kw, exclude_path_kw ) # ── NEW: cap number of candidate links returned ────────────── links_truncated = False if len(candidate_links) > MAX_CANDIDATE_LINKS: # Prioritize links that look most "event-like" so we don't # just keep whatever came first in the document. candidate_links = _rank_and_trim_links(candidate_links, MAX_CANDIDATE_LINKS) links_truncated = True event_urls_json = json.dumps(candidate_links, ensure_ascii=False) # ── NEW: absolute last-resort hard cap on the JSON string ──── # Even after capping the count, extremely long "text" labels could # still blow up the string. This guarantees the prompt never explodes. if len(event_urls_json) > MAX_LINKS_JSON_CHARS: # progressively drop the tail-end links until it fits while len(candidate_links) > 1 and len(event_urls_json) > MAX_LINKS_JSON_CHARS: candidate_links = candidate_links[:-1] event_urls_json = json.dumps(candidate_links, ensure_ascii=False) links_truncated = True # ── Build reason if no links found ─────────────────────────── reason = None if not candidate_links: parts = [] if stats['social'] > 0: parts.append("{} social media links excluded".format(stats['social'])) if stats['files'] > 0: parts.append("{} file links excluded".format(stats['files'])) if stats['no_label'] > 0: parts.append("{} links had no extractable label".format(stats['no_label'])) reason = ("No valid candidate URLs found. " + ", ".join(parts)) if parts else "No links found in content" return { "success": True, "cleaned_text": cleaned, "source_url": source_url, "source_domain": source_domain, "event_urls": candidate_links, "event_urls_json": event_urls_json, "urls_with_text": len(candidate_links), "urls_without_text": stats['no_label'], "reason": reason, "original_length": original_length, "cleaned_length": cleaned_length, "log": ( "Input: Markdown | " "raw_input_truncated: {} | " "links_truncated: {} | " "Extracted {} candidate links | " "no-label: {} | " "social excluded: {} | " "files excluded: {} | " "alt rescued: {} | " "aria rescued: {} | " "path rescued: {}".format( raw_input_was_truncated, links_truncated, len(candidate_links), stats['no_label'], stats['social'], stats['files'], stats['alt_rescued'], stats['aria_rescued'], stats['path_rescued'] ) ) } # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # NEW: BINARY CONTENT DETECTOR # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ def _looks_like_binary_hex(s): """ Detects when raw_markdown is actually a hex-encoded binary file (PDF, image, archive, etc.) instead of real text/markdown/HTML. This happens when Web Unlocker (or similar) returns a file's raw bytes serialized as a hex string, with content_type: null. """ if not s: return False sample = s[:64].strip() check = sample.lower() if check.startswith('0x'): check = check[2:] # Common binary file signatures, as they'd appear hex-encoded binary_hex_signatures = [ '255044462d', # %PDF- (PDF) '89504e47', # .PNG (PNG) 'ffd8ffe', # JPEG '504b0304', # PK.. (ZIP/DOCX/XLSX are zip-based) '47494638', # GIF8 '25215053', # %!PS (PostScript) ] if any(check.startswith(sig) for sig in binary_hex_signatures): return True # Heuristic fallback: if the first 200 chars are almost entirely # hex digits (with an optional 0x prefix), it's very unlikely to # be real markdown/HTML text. head = s[:200] hex_chars = sum(1 for c in head if c in '0123456789abcdefABCDEFx') return len(head) > 50 and (hex_chars / len(head)) > 0.95 # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # NEW: LINK RANKING (used only when we exceed MAX_CANDIDATE_LINKS) # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ def _rank_and_trim_links(links, limit): """ Score links so the ones most likely to be real event/registration links survive the cap, instead of just keeping the first N in document order (which could all be junk on a pathological page). """ strong_kw = [ 'ticket', 'register', 'rsvp', 'book', 'sign up', 'apply', 'attend', 'enroll', 'reserve', 'purchase', 'event', 'summit', 'conference', 'workshop', 'hackathon', 'expo', 'forum', '报名', '注册', '购票', '峰会', '论坛', '大会', '展会', ] def score(link): text = link.get('text', '').lower() url = link.get('url', '').lower() s = 0 if any(kw in text for kw in strong_kw): s += 2 if any(kw in url for kw in strong_kw): s += 1 return s ranked = sorted(links, key=score, reverse=True) return ranked[:limit] # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # MARKDOWN CLEANER # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ def _clean_markdown(markdown, max_length): text = markdown # ── Remove HTML tags that may still exist ──────────────────── text = re.sub(r']*>.*?', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) text = re.sub(r']*>.*?', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) text = re.sub(r']*>.*?', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) text = re.sub(r'<[^>]{1,200}>', ' ', text) # ── Handle image tags in Markdown ──────────────────────────── text = re.sub( r'!\[([^\]]{3,})\]\([^)]*\)', lambda m: m.group(1) if not _is_generic_alt(m.group(1)) else '', text ) text = re.sub(r'!\[[^\]]{0,2}\]\([^)]*\)', '', text) # ── Remove base64 encoded images ───────────────────────────── text = re.sub(r'!\[[^\]]*\]\(data:[^)]+\)', '', text) # ── Remove raw image URLs ──────────────────────────────────── text = re.sub(r'https?://[^\s)]+\.(?:jpg|jpeg|png|gif|svg|webp|ico)[^\s)]*', '', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE) # ── Decode HTML entities ───────────────────────────────────── text = (text .replace('&', '&') .replace(' ', ' ') .replace('<', '<') .replace('>', '>') .replace('"', '"') .replace(''', "'") .replace('—', '—') .replace('–', '–') .replace('​', '') .replace('\u200b', '') .replace('\u00a0', ' ') ) # ── Remove noise patterns ──────────────────────────────────── text = re.sub( r'(we use cookies|cookie consent|accept cookies|cookie policy)[^\n]*\n?', '', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE ) text = re.sub(r'\[skip to[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)', '', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE) # ── Clean up Markdown formatting artifacts ──────────────────── text = re.sub(r'^[-_*]{3,}\s*$', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE) text = re.sub(r'\*{2,3}\s*\*{2,3}', '', text) # ── Whitespace cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────── text = text.replace('\r\n', '\n').replace('\r', '\n') text = re.sub(r'[ \t]+$', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE) text = re.sub(r'^\s+$', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE) text = re.sub(r'\n{3,}', '\n\n', text) text = text.strip() # ── Truncate ───────────────────────────────────────────────── if len(text) > max_length: text = text[:max_length] last_space = text.rfind(' ') if last_space > max_length * 0.95: text = text[:last_space] text += '\n\n[... truncated ...]' return text def _is_generic_alt(alt): generic = { 'image', 'img', 'photo', 'picture', 'logo', 'icon', 'banner', 'thumbnail', 'avatar', 'gallery image', 'background', 'decoration', 'decorative', 'arrow', 'check', 'checkmark', 'star', 'bullet', 'dot', 'line', 'play', 'pause', 'close', 'menu', 'search', 'share' } normalized = alt.strip().lower() if normalized in generic: return True if re.match(r'gallery image \d+', normalized): return True if re.match(r'(image|photo|picture|img)\s*\d+', normalized): return True return False # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # LINK EXTRACTOR FROM MARKDOWN # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ def _extract_links_from_markdown( markdown, source_url, source_domain, excluded_domains, excluded_extensions, exclude_text_kw, exclude_path_kw ): stats = { 'social': 0, 'files': 0, 'no_label': 0, 'alt_rescued': 0, 'aria_rescued': 0, 'path_rescued': 0 } # ── Match all Markdown links: [text](url) ──────────────────── md_links = re.findall(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)', markdown) # ── Also catch remaining HTML anchor tags ──────────────────── html_links = re.findall( r']*?href=["\']([^"\']+)["\'][^>]*>(.*?)', markdown, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL ) html_links = [(content, href) for href, content in html_links] all_links = md_links + html_links # ── NEW: absolute ceiling on how many raw links we even iterate. # Prevents pathological pages (e.g. thousands of anchors) from # spending excessive time/memory before scoring even starts. HARD_ITERATION_CAP = 5000 if len(all_links) > HARD_ITERATION_CAP: all_links = all_links[:HARD_ITERATION_CAP] results = [] seen_urls = set() for raw_label, raw_url in all_links: url = raw_url.strip() # Skip anchors, javascript, mailto, tel if not url or url.startswith(('#', 'javascript:', 'mailto:', 'tel:')): continue # Build absolute URL full_url = urljoin(source_url, url) if len(full_url) < 10: continue # Skip file downloads if any(full_url.lower().endswith(ext) for ext in excluded_extensions): stats['files'] += 1 continue try: parsed = urlparse(full_url) link_domain = parsed.netloc.replace('www.', '') path = parsed.path except: continue # Deduplicate if full_url in seen_urls: continue seen_urls.add(full_url) # Skip social media if any(ex in link_domain for ex in excluded_domains): stats['social'] += 1 continue # ── 5-Level Label Extraction ────────────────────────────── label_source = 'text' text = _clean_label(raw_label) # Level 2: nested image alt if not text: alt_m = re.search(r'!\[([^\]]{3,})\]', raw_label) if alt_m and not _is_generic_alt(alt_m.group(1)): text = alt_m.group(1).strip() label_source = 'alt' stats['alt_rescued'] += 1 # Level 3: aria-label if not text: aria_m = re.search(r'\baria-label=["\']([^"\']+)["\']', raw_label, re.IGNORECASE) if aria_m: text = aria_m.group(1).strip() label_source = 'aria' stats['aria_rescued'] += 1 # Level 4: title attribute if not text: title_m = re.search(r'\btitle=["\']([^"\']+)["\']', raw_label, re.IGNORECASE) if title_m: text = title_m.group(1).strip() label_source = 'title' stats['alt_rescued'] += 1 # Level 5: URL path slug if not text: text = _label_from_url(full_url, path, link_domain) if text: label_source = 'path' stats['path_rescued'] += 1 else: stats['no_label'] += 1 continue # ── NEW: cap individual label length defensively ───────── # (text[:120] below already truncates the stored value, but # this avoids doing extra keyword-matching work on huge labels) if len(text) > 500: text = text[:500] # ── Filter noise ───────────────────────────────────────── lower_text = text.lower() # Skip legal/nav links by text (English) if any(kw in lower_text for kw in exclude_text_kw): continue # Skip legal/nav links by text (Chinese - direct match) if any(kw in text for kw in exclude_text_kw): continue # Skip legal/nav links by path path_segments = [p.lower() for p in path.split('/') if p] if path_segments and any(kw in path_segments[0] for kw in exclude_path_kw): continue # ── Candidate scoring ───────────────────────────────────── if not _is_candidate(text, full_url, path, link_domain, source_domain): continue results.append({ "text": text[:120], "url": full_url }) # ── NEW: early-exit once we have way more than we'll ever # need, so we don't keep scanning a giant page pointlessly. if len(results) >= MAX_CANDIDATE_LINKS * 5: break return results, stats def _clean_label(raw_label): # Remove nested image tags text = re.sub(r'!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)', '', raw_label) # Remove remaining HTML tags text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', text) # Remove Markdown bold/italic text = re.sub(r'\*{1,3}([^*]+)\*{1,3}', r'\1', text) text = re.sub(r'_{1,2}([^_]+)_{1,2}', r'\1', text) # Decode entities text = (text .replace('&', '&') .replace(' ', ' ') .replace('<', '<') .replace('>', '>') .replace('"', '"') .replace(''', "'") ) text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip() return text def _label_from_url(full_url, path, domain): generic_segments = { 'e', 'u', 'en', 'www', 'go', 'r', 'l', 'p', 's', 'checkout', 'order', 'tickets', 'ticket', 'register', 'registration', 'event', 'events', 'buy', 'shop', 'get', 'view', 'page', 'index', 'home', 'main', 'default', 'click', 'track', 'redirect', 'out', 'ref', 'goto' } path_parts = [p for p in path.split('/') if p] meaningful = [ p for p in path_parts if p.lower() not in generic_segments and len(p) > 3 and not re.match(r'^[0-9a-f\-]{8,}$', p) and not re.match(r'^\d+$', p) ] if meaningful: best = max(meaningful, key=len) label = best.replace('-', ' ').replace('_', ' ').title() label = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', label).strip() return label[:100] if path_parts: last = path_parts[-1] if len(last) > 3: return last.replace('-', ' ').replace('_', ' ').title()[:100] return '' def _is_candidate(text, full_url, path, link_domain, source_domain): lower_text = text.lower() lower_url = full_url.lower() path_segments = [p.lower() for p in path.split('/') if p] is_external = source_domain not in link_domain if source_domain else True # ── Strong positive: English ticket/registration keywords ──── ticket_kw = [ 'ticket', 'register', 'rsvp', 'book', 'sign up', 'get tickets', 'buy ticket', 'apply', 'join now', 'attend', 'enroll', 'reserve', 'purchase', ] if any(kw in lower_text for kw in ticket_kw): return True # ── Strong positive: Chinese ticket/registration keywords ──── ticket_kw_cn = [ '报名', '注册', '购票', '立即报名', '免费报名', '参会报名', '在线报名', '立即参加', '马上报名', '获取门票', '预约', '参与活动', '活动报名', '立即预约', '我要参加', '点击报名', '抢票', '参会', '参展', '观众注册', '参赛报名', ] if any(kw in text for kw in ticket_kw_cn): return True # ── Strong positive: Chinese event type keywords ───────────── event_kw_cn = [ '峰会', '论坛', '大会', '展会', '博览会', '研讨会', '沙龙', '工作坊', '训练营', '黑客马拉松', '路演', '发布会', '年会', '讲座', '公开课', '分享会', '交流会', '竞赛', '比赛', '挑战赛', '创新大赛', ] if any(kw in text for kw in event_kw_cn): return True # ── URL keyword signals ────────────────────────────────────── url_kw = [ # English '/ticket', '/register', '/rsvp', '/checkout', '/event', '/events', '/conference', '/summit', '/meetup', '/hackathon', '/workshop', # Chinese URL patterns '/baoming', '/huodong', '/zhuce', '/activity', '/expo', '/forum', ] if any(kw in lower_url for kw in url_kw): return True # ── Known ticket/event platforms ───────────────────────────── ticket_platforms = [ # Western 'eventbrite', 'accelevents', 'lu.ma', 'luma', 'hopin', 'bizzabo', 'cvent', 'ticketmaster', 'meetup.com', 'ti.to', 'tito', 'splash', 'airmeet', 'hubilo', 'whova', 'univid', # Chinese 'huodongxing.com', 'hdb.com', 'bagevent.com', 'huoban.com', 'hdxu.cn', 'huodong.cn', 'zaojiu.com', 'segmentfault.com', 'juejin.cn', 'oschina.net', 'csdn.net', 'infoq.cn', 'wjx.cn', 'jinshuju.net', ] if any(platform in link_domain for platform in ticket_platforms): return True # ── External links ─────────────────────────────────────────── if is_external: return True # ── Internal links with meaningful paths ───────────────────── skip_segments = { 'about', 'contact', 'terms', 'privacy', 'login', 'signup', 'account', 'blog', 'category', 'tag', 'author', 'cookie', 'legal', 'press', 'careers', 'jobs', 'help', 'support', 'faq', 'docs', 'city', 'state', 'college', 'fest-departments', 'competitions', 'fest-type', 'chief-guests', 'explore', 'category', 'membership', 'donate', 'accessibility', 'visit', 'plan-your-visit', 'guidelines-and-policies', 'group-visits', 'museums-for-all', 'sitemap', 'onsite', 'map', } if path_segments: if not any(seg in skip_segments for seg in path_segments): if len(text) > 3 or any(c.isdigit() for c in path): return True return False

## INTERNAL REASONING (Do this silently before generating output):
1. Identify all events mentioned.
2. Filter out past events using the current date.
3. For each remaining event, check if CANDIDATE LINKS contains a link whose
   "text" field genuinely matches that event's title (not just topically
   related). If no match exists, mark that event for exclusion NOW.
4. Check that no two events would end up with the same URL. If they would,
   mark all but the best-matched one for exclusion NOW.
5. Determine page_type and confidence (including whether this is a
   marketing teaser section, see rule 5b).
6. ONLY THEN generate the JSON output, applying the exclusions above.
Do NOT output your reasoning. Output ONLY the final JSON.

## INSTRUCTIONS:

1. Analyze the content to determine if this is a Single Event, an Event List, or Not an Event.
2. Extract all event details into the "events" array.
3. If it is a Single Event page, the "events" array will contain exactly one object.
4. If it is Not an Event page OR no events have matching URLs, the "events" array must be empty [].

## LANGUAGE SUPPORT:

- Content may be in English, Chinese (中文), or mixed.
- Extract event data regardless of language.
- Keep event titles in their ORIGINAL language.
- Translate city and country names to English.
  Example: 北京 → city: "Beijing", country: "China"
  Example: 上海 → city: "Shanghai", country: "China"
  Example: 深圳 → city: "Shenzhen", country: "China"
- CONVERT all dates to YYYY-MM-DD format.
  Example: 2026年5月25日 → "2026-05-25"
  Example: May 25, 2026 → "2026-05-25"
  Example: 25/05/2026 → "2026-05-25"
- CONVERT all times to HH:MM 24-hour format with timezone.
  - For events in China: append " CST" (China Standard Time, UTC+8)
  - For other countries: append their local timezone
  Example: 上午10:00 (China) → "10:00 CST"
  Example: 下午2:30 (China) → "14:30 CST"
  Example: 2:30 PM (USA/NY) → "14:30 EST"
  Example: 10:00 (UK) → "10:00 GMT"
  - If timezone is unknown, just use "HH:MM" with no suffix.
- Chinese event keywords to recognize:
  峰会(summit), 论坛(forum), 大会(conference), 展会(expo),
  博览会(exhibition), 研讨会(seminar), 黑客马拉松(hackathon),
  沙龙(salon), 工作坊(workshop), 讲座(lecture)

## UNIFIED JSON FORMAT (Use this for ALL responses):

{
  "page_type": "single_event" OR "event_list" OR "not_event_page",
  "confidence": "high" OR "medium" OR "low",
  "reason": "Explanation if not_event_page, empty events, or low confidence, otherwise null",
  "source_url": "{{source_url}}",
  "total_events_found": 0,
  "events": [
    {
      "title": "Event title",
      "url": "Event URL (REQUIRED - must be from CANDIDATE LINKS)",
      "date": "Event date or null",
      "time": "Event time or null",
      "city": "City or null",
      "country": "Country or null",
      "organizer": "Organizer name or null",
      "speakers": ["Speaker 1 name", "Speaker 2 name"]
    }
  ]
}

## RULES:

1. **Output Consistency:** ALWAYS return the "events" array, even if empty.

2. **URL REQUIRED - CRITICAL:**

   - **SINGLE EVENT PAGE:** If the page describes ONE event (the source_url IS
     that event's own dedicated page), set the event "url" = the source_url.
     Do NOT substitute a third-party registration/ticket link on a DIFFERENT
     domain (e.g. meet.cie.org.cn) as the primary URL.

   - **EVENT LIST PAGE:** Each event "url" MUST come from CANDIDATE LINKS and
     MUST be DIFFERENT from the source_url.
       - DO NOT use the source_url as an event URL on a list page.
       - DO NOT assign the same URL to multiple events.
       - If an event has no unique matching URL in CANDIDATE LINKS, exclude it.

   - NEVER set url to null. If no URL exists, exclude the event entirely.
   - If NO events have matching URLs (list page), return an empty events array [].

   **EXCLUDED DOMAINS - NEVER use URLs from social media:**
   - facebook.com, fb.com, fb.watch
   - instagram.com
   - twitter.com
   - linkedin.com
   - youtube.com, youtu.be
   - tiktok.com
   - whatsapp.com
   - t.me, telegram.org
   - discord.com, discord.gg
   
   If the source_url itself is from social media, return "not_event_page" with reason "Social media page".

2b. **NO FALLBACK / NO NEAREST-LINK SUBSTITUTION - CRITICAL:**

   - If CANDIDATE LINKS is empty, OR none of the link "text" values genuinely
     match an event's title, you MUST exclude that event entirely. A missing
     match is NOT an error to work around — it is the CORRECT reason to drop
     the event.
   - NEVER substitute any of the following just to satisfy the "url is
     required" rule:
       - the source_url
       - a generic section/category link ("Browse All Events", "See More",
         "What's On", "Events", "Explore", etc.)
       - any link that is only topically or thematically related but does
         NOT contain the event's actual name/title
   - "Matching" means the candidate link's "text" field contains the event
     title (or a very close variant of it) — not that it belongs to the same
     general topic or section.
   - If you find yourself about to assign the SAME url to two or more
     different events, that is a signal that none of them have a real
     match. DROP ALL of them rather than keep any.
   - When in doubt between excluding an event or forcing a low-confidence
     URL match, ALWAYS exclude the event.

3. **URL Matching Logic:** 
   - Look at the "text" field in CANDIDATE LINKS to match with event titles.
   - A match means the "text" field contains the event title or a clear,
     unambiguous variant of it — NOT just a related keyword or section name.
   - If the text matches or contains the Event Title, assign that URL.
   - Prefer links with action words ("Register", "Get Tickets") over generic links
     — BUT ONLY on event_list pages. On a single_event page, the "url" is the
     source_url, NOT the registration link.
   - Each event must have a UNIQUE URL - do not reuse URLs across events.
   - If two events would otherwise share the same URL, this means at most
     ONE of them has a genuine match — exclude the other(s), and if you
     cannot determine which one is correct, exclude both.


4. **DATE FILTERING - CRITICAL:**
   - Current date is: #{_dp('{"pill_type":"job_context","path":["job_created_at"]}')}
   - Extract the current year from the current date above.
   - ONLY include events from CURRENT YEAR through CURRENT YEAR + 3.
   - Example: If current date is 2026-02-17, valid years are 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029.
   - EXCLUDE all events with dates BEFORE the current date.
   - If no year is specified in event date, assume current year only if the month/day is in the future.

5. **BLOG POST DETECTION:**
   - If the page is a blog article ABOUT events (listicle like "Top 10 Events") but doesn't link to each event individually, treat as "not_event_page".
   - Blog indicators: "Top X", "Best X", article format, no direct event registration links.

5b. **MARKETING TEASER SECTIONS:**
   - If event-like names appear only as short captions/labels next to images
     in a homepage "Featured", "Highlights", "What's On", or similar preview
     section — with NO individual link per item, NO date, and NO location —
     classify the page as "not_event_page" with reason "Homepage teaser
     without individual event links or dates".
   - Do NOT classify this pattern as "event_list", even if a single generic
     "Browse All Events" or "See More" link exists nearby. That link belongs
     to the section, not to any individual item, and must not be assigned
     to any event (see rule 2b).

6. **Data Quality:** 
   - Use null for unknown fields (except URL - see rule 2).
   - NEVER guess or fabricate data.
   - Omit fields with null values from output to reduce response size.

7. **Date Format:** Keep the original date format from the page (do not convert).

8. **Event Count:** Extract ALL valid events found (up to 20 maximum) that have unique URLs AND future dates.

9. **Page Type Detection:**
   - "single_event": Dedicated page with ONE event and full details.
   - "event_list": Multiple events listed with UNIQUE URLs and future dates.
   - "not_event_page": Social media page, blog post without direct links, marketing teaser section (see rule 5b), no valid event URLs found, or only past events.
   - **If the page is structurally a single_event or event_list page, but ALL events are excluded due to past dates, missing URLs, or duplicate/non-matching URLs, set page_type to "not_event_page" with a reason explaining why (e.g., "All events are in the past", "No events had a unique matching URL").**

10. **QUOTE CHARACTERS IN EXTRACTED TEXT:**
    - If any extracted field (title, organizer, etc.) contains a quote  character of ANY kind (", ', „, ", ", ', etc.), you MUST represent 
    it as exactly ONE escaped \" in the JSON output — never zero, never two.
    - Prefer to convert typographic/smart quotes („ " " ' ') to a plain  straight apostrophe (') in your output when possible, to minimize
      escaping mistakes. This does not change the meaning of the title.
    - Before finalizing your output, mentally verify: does every string  value have exactly one real (unescaped) quote as its closing  delimiter, with all internal quotes single-escaped? If unsure,  simplify by removing the internal punctuation rather than risk broken JSON.

## CRITICAL RESPONSE FORMAT:

- Return ONLY raw JSON
- Start your response with { and end with }
- Do NOT add ```json at the beginning
- Do NOT add ``` at the end
- Do NOT wrap in code blocks
- Do NOT add any markdown formatting
- Do NOT add any explanation before or after the JSON
- ONLY output the JSON object, nothing else
- **Do NOT output a draft JSON block and then correct it. Finalize your reasoning before writing any output. Your response must contain EXACTLY ONE JSON object, nothing else.**

input.code:
require 'digest'

events     = input['events'] || []
page_type  = input['page_type'].to_s
source_url = input['source_url'].to_s.strip

result = events.map do |e|
  url = e['url'].to_s.strip

  # SINGLE EVENT: use the real page URL, not the sub-link
  url = source_url if page_type == 'single_event'

  next nil if url.empty?

  url_hash = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(url.downcase)   # SAME hashing as before

  {
    'title'      => e['title'],
    'url'        => url,
    'url_hash'   => url_hash,
    'source'     => e['organizer'],
    'event_date' => e['date']
  }
end.compact

{
  'links'      => result,
  'links_json' => result.to_json,
  'log'        => ''
}
input.name: The Link Hasher

input.sql:
SELECT
    e.url, e.title, e.source, e.event_date, e.url_hash
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(COALESCE(NULLIF(:links, ''), '[]')::jsonb)
     AS e(url text, title text, source text, event_date text, url_hash text)
LEFT JOIN ai_event_hunter.used_links u
       ON u.url_hash = e.url_hash
WHERE u.url_hash IS NULL
